sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Anscombe Diagnostic Studio! Select Datasets 1, 2, 3, or 4 from the dropdown. Compare the Ordinary Least Squares line in dashed red with the robust Theil-Sen fit in green, and inspect the residual stem plot below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the dataset selector, Nova! When I pick Dataset 2, the residual stems form a perfect parabola, exposing the quadratic law that summary moments hid!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: In linear regression, why does Ordinary Least Squares have a breakdown point of zero percent while Theil-Sen achieves approximately 29.3 percent? Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: A zero percent breakdown point versus twenty-nine percent! Review our three options above me and select the correct mathematical mechanism!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! Because Ordinary Least Squares minimizes squared residuals, a single distant point exerts leverage proportional to x squared, tilting the slope arbitrarily. Theil-Sen evaluates the median of all pairwise slopes, requiring nearly thirty percent of points to be corrupted before the median breaks down!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Remember that breakdown point measures resistance to adversarial leverage points. Ordinary Least Squares collapses under a single extreme leverage point due to quadratic penalty summation, whereas Theil-Sen takes the median of pairwise slopes.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Tukey Decomposition Workbench! Tweak the smoother window width k and inject impulse outlier spikes. Watch how the moving median smoother protects the fit, while extracted residuals isolate the spikes cleanly!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the smoother controls, Nova! When I inject four extreme spikes, the moving median curve ignores them completely, and the Durbin-Watson gauge tracks white noise!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: An analyst tests eighty covariates without pre-registration, finds one with p equals 0.012, and declares it statistically significant. What statistical pathology is this, and what is the proper production defense protocol? Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Eighty candidate features and a p-value of 0.012! Review our three options above me and select the proper statistical protocol!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely right! This is the Garden of Forking Paths. Across eighty independent pure-noise variables, the probability of observing at least one spuriously significant correlation at alpha equals 0.05 is over ninety-eight percent! The proper defense is split verification: uncover candidates freely on an exploratory partition, then evaluate significance once strictly on a frozen confirmatory holdout.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Conducting confirmatory significance testing on hypotheses suggested by the same exploratory dataset destroys p-value validity through researcher degrees of freedom. The rigorous protocol is to split data into an exploratory partition and a frozen confirmatory holdout.
